text: What Isaac knows is not told in Genesis 22. He bears the wood, asks after the lamb, and receives from Abraham a reply which evades the matter it seems to meet. Of Isaac's inward thought or fear the narrator gives nothing; he records only that they went, both of them, together. The phrase returns, and its return supplies the place of explanation. Consent is thereby brought into view, and as quietly dismissed; the logic of obedience settles everything, and leaves nothing unaccounted for.
